newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 97/98 soybean ending stocks critical - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97/98 soybean ending stocks critical - Safras.

text.p: Brazil 1997/98 soybean ending stocks should drop to a critically low 298,000 tonnes, down 29 percent on the previous year, as demand sharply outpaces supply, independent consultants Safras e Mercado projected.

"The external market has every reason to believe that Brazil will have little product to negotiate from now on and that it will still be a potential buyer, mainly for the period after October when domestic offer is forecast to end," Safras said.

Soybean stocks for the 1997/98 marketing year (February-January) were estimated at 12.6 million tonnes on July 1, down from 13.5 million tonnes at the same time last year, Safras said in a weekly report.

"If on one side total offer shows growth of around seven percent over the previous year, consumption grew more than proportionally by...22 percent, fruit of the explosion of soybean exports and the acceleration of crushing," Safras said.
The internal market was already showing the shortages characteristic of the gap in between harvests, with local supply totally dependent on imports, the report said.
By June 26, farmers had already committed 84 percent of the total expected 1996/97 harvest of 26.02 million tonnes, up from 79 percent at the same time last year, Safras estimated.

"In general, producers are reticent to sell what they still have of the old crop, precisely with the expectation that this absence of product in the internal market will push prices even higher," it said.
Prices were 15 to 22 percent above the 10-year average for June and between 34 and 47 percent higher than during June 1996, Safras said.
